correctness.rationale: For the specified state-dependent transition law, iteration gives log2|z_n| = 2^n(t-R_n), with t=log2 r. At t=R the scaled remaining tail lies in [0,1], so there is no escape; every coding cylinder has mass at most (1-eps)^n and the at-most-two expansions of a point give no atoms. Hence endpoint threshold conventions do not affect either exact identity. On the upper and lower endpoint intervals of width 2^-n in t, the forced prefixes are respectively n ones and n zeros; subtract the prefix and rescale the tail. The two deterministic runs saturate after at most any N such that (1-alpha)^N(1-eps)<=eps, uniformly in p. Their masses then factor into the displayed positive prefactors times (1-eps)^n. Digit/state complementation identifies the two tails; for phases u in [1/2,1] the common profile is in [1-eps,1], yielding uniform sharp bounds, with the radial changes of variable having nonzero endpoint derivatives. At alpha=1/2, eps=1/4 the probability of the prefix 01 is 3/32, giving H(3/4)=27/32; (3/4)^log2(4/3) > sqrt(3)/2 > 27/32, giving distinct normalized subsequential limits. The finite-cylinder checker is supplementary, not a replacement for these arguments.
